tweets.text:
.@DavidDeutschOxf on why the people in favor of regulating AI are wrong:

“They look at problems and they think they’re insoluble because they haven’t been solved, and therefore they want to prevent the progress that is going to cause the problems.

Now, generically, what that will do is it will make the progress happen in the wrong place.

It will happen among people who do not obey the regulation, and those people are people who are alienated from the best culture, and they will then become a danger to the best culture.

Now, I’m speaking in general terms about progress—progress in computing and so on—but I think this particular thing you’ve mentioned is actually not going to be that much of a danger.

AGI (artificial general intelligence) will present a whole load of new problems which will have to be solved, no doubt with the help of AGI.

But AI, the kind of thing we have now with ChatGPT and that kind of thing, which is amazingly and increasingly useful and is going to have unpredictable effects on society—most of them good—isn’t anything profound.

It’s no different from having a calculator or a slide rule.”
